# Probable Cause While actively enforcing the law, officers are held to the standard of Probable Cause. This phrase represents a reasonable suspicion that a crime has very recently been committed, or is currently underway, and does not require the officer to have forensic evidence of criminal activity. Examples of Probable Cause include an officer witnessing a crime being committed firsthand, or multiple corroborating eyewitness reports on a suspect that has reasonable ability to perform the reported crime and was confirmed to be at the location of the crime.
When judged, Probable Cause is to be interpreted within the context of the entirety of the station’s circumstances at the time of the incident. Probable Cause negates the need of a warrant for non-implant searches, and, once concluded, is to be promptly reported to the Prosecutor, Warden, or Head of Security for review.
